messages:
maria (docs): FYI I opened a PR that reorganizes the function-invoke examples and standardizes the 'response envelope' pattern we recommend for tool calls. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/462

sam (eng-runtime): Thanks. Quick question — are we keeping the JSON schema as a required top-level `result` field or switching to an envelope where result can be null and an `error` object exists?

maria (docs): Going with envelope: {
  \"status\": \"ok|error\",
  \"result\": <typed payload or null>,
  \"error\": {\"code\":..., \"message\":...} | null
}

kevin (devex): That matches conversational fallback patterns we've seen. Can we include both Python and Node snippets showing parse+guard? I noticed some old snippets still use ad-hoc parsing.

maria (docs): Yep — added both. Example (Python):
```python
resp = client.call_tool(name='extract_price', input=text)
if resp['status'] != 'ok':
    raise RuntimeError(resp['error']['message'])
payload = resp['result']  # validated against JSON schema
```

luis (eng-ml): Small note: for quantized models we need to warn about token truncation leading to partial JSON. Maybe add a short guard section on resilient parsing and KV-cache edge cases.

maria (docs): Good catch. I added a "robust parsing" blurb with strategies: partial-JSON backoff, retry with higher max_tokens, and a pointer to the parse-fallback RFC.

sam (eng-runtime): Also can you add a short perf note: prefer streamed tokens for large structured outputs but add a final integrity check when reassembling before JSON.parse. Example: join chunks -> validate against schema.

kevin (devex): I left inline comments on a couple of examples where we still show `eval()` parsing — that's unsafe, please replace with json.loads/json.parse and schema validation callouts.

maria (docs): Replaced eval() usages. Also added a `jq` one-liner for maintainers in the debugging section.

maria (docs): Question for @sam: in the SDK example I used `call_tool` name + schema arg. Do we want to align with the new SDK signature `call_tool(name, schema=...)` or keep `schema` in options dict?

sam (eng-runtime): We landed on `call_tool(name, schema=..., validate=True)` in the last SDK PR. Use that and I can patch runtime glue if anything mismatches.

kevin (devex): Can someone run a quick link sweep? I saw one doc still points to the old "parser guide v1" URL.

maria (docs): I did a pass but manual sweep would be great. Please leave line comments on the PR. Hoping to merge by EOD if no blockers. :pray:

deploy-bot: Reminder — docs CI will run link-check + schema-lint on merge.

luis (eng-ml): I'll review the guardrail language for edge cases (truncated arrays, optional union types). Won't block unless there are semantic issues.

sam (eng-runtime): I can do a quick SDK smoke test after kevin's devex review. If all green, approve.

kevin (devex): Reviewing now, will ping inline.

maria (docs): Thanks everyone — leaving small checklist in the PR: update SDK signature, remove eval(), add parse-fallback examples, link-sweep. Ping me once reviews are in and I'll merge.
